title: Design a reviewer-friendly analytics repository
outcomes: Separate raw, interim and curated data.
Make project structure navigable without opening every file.
Keep generated outputs reproducible and avoid committing environments or secrets.
tasks: Create a repository with README, data/raw, data/processed, src, sql, reports, tests and docs.
Add a data dictionary and source provenance note.
Add .gitignore for virtual environments, caches, credentials and local databases containing sensitive data.
Keep synthetic sample data small; document where full data comes from.
acceptance: A reviewer can identify purpose, inputs, outputs and run steps in under two minutes.
No credentials, PHI, real patient data or environment folders are committed.
File names and paths are consistent and portable.

title: Write an evidence-based README
outcomes: Describe the business question and audience.
Document reproducibility and validation.
Separate findings from assumptions and limitations.
tasks: Write project title, business context, scope and dataset grain.
Document setup, exact commands, expected outputs and software versions.
Include metric definitions, QA checks, key findings, limitations and screenshots/figures where safe.
Add a synthetic-data/privacy statement and attribution/licensing.
acceptance: No unsupported impact claims.
Commands are complete and paths exist.
Every displayed metric has a definition and denominator.
Limitations are explicit.

title: Git workflow and meaningful commit history
outcomes: Use status, diff, log, branch, commit and remote safely.
Keep commits small and descriptive.
Avoid committing secrets or patient information.
tasks: Initialise a local repository; inspect status before staging.
Use a feature branch for one improvement.
Review git diff; stage selected files; commit with imperative message.
Create a .gitignore; scan staged diff for PHI/secrets before push.
Use a remote only after reviewing repository visibility and data permissions.
acceptance: Working tree is understood before each commit.
No blind git add of sensitive exports.
Commit history communicates project evolution.
Remote visibility is intentional.

title: Code quality, tests and reproducibility
outcomes: Separate reusable functions from notebook-only logic.
Add deterministic checks and data contracts.
Capture environment and execution evidence.
tasks: Refactor repeated transformations into functions.
Add schema, uniqueness, range and reconciliation tests.
Set random seeds for synthetic demonstrations.
Record dependency versions and exact run command.
Capture clean-run logs and expected outputs.
acceptance: A fresh environment can reproduce results.
Tests fail when a deliberate defect is introduced.
Warnings and exceptions are reviewed, not hidden.
No machine-specific absolute paths.

title: Analytical code review and pull-request practice
outcomes: Review correctness, grain, denominators, missingness and clinical claims.
Write actionable review comments.
Respond to feedback with traceable changes.
tasks: Review a peer's SQL/Python against the checklist.
Identify one correctness risk, one maintainability issue and one documentation gap.
Write comments with file/line, impact and suggested correction.
Revise code and document what changed.
acceptance: Comments are specific, respectful and reproducible.
Review distinguishes blocking defects from suggestions.
Author response closes each issue with evidence.

title: Portfolio narrative and project selection
outcomes: Select projects aligned with role requirements.
Explain personal contribution and analytical judgement.
Present evidence without exaggerating experience.
tasks: Select 2–3 strongest projects for a target job family.
Write a concise case study for each: problem, approach, tools, QA, result, limitations.
Map every CV claim to an inspectable artefact.
Prepare a 90-second spoken walkthrough.
acceptance: Claims match evidence and role level.
Projects demonstrate different capabilities, not duplicate dashboards.
Synthetic work is labelled as synthetic.

title: Technical interview: SQL, Python and statistics
outcomes: Explain and solve timed analytical tasks.
Communicate assumptions before coding.
Validate outputs and discuss alternatives.
tasks: Complete the supplied timed SQL and Python interview bank.
Explain join cardinality and denominator choice aloud.
Interpret uncertainty and avoid causal overreach.
Review edge cases and propose tests.
acceptance: Correct answer plus explanation.
Explicit assumptions and data grain.
Validation and limitations included.

title: Remote client interview and delivery simulation
outcomes: Clarify ambiguous requests.
Manage scope, risks and deadlines.
Deliver concise async updates and handoffs.
tasks: Conduct a mock intake using client prompts.
Write a scope confirmation and risk escalation.
Send a midpoint update with blockers and revised ETA.
Deliver files with reproducibility, QA and limitations.
acceptance: No silent assumptions on key metrics.
Risks raised early with options.
Handoff can be reproduced by another analyst.
